_README: Pesticides banned, withdrawn or restricted in India, from the Central
Insecticides Board and Registration Committee list as tabled in
Parliament. Verified against the source named in verified_from on the
The three categories are kept apart on purpose, because collapsing them
is itself misinformation. Monocrotophos is not banned in India: it is
banned on vegetables and legal elsewhere. Telling a cotton grower that
the product in their shed is illegal is wrong, and being wrong in that
direction costs trust that the genuinely banned entries depend on.
RE-CHECK PERIODICALLY. The Registration Committee reviews and adds to
this list. A missing entry means a farmer is not warned; a wrong entry
means they are warned about something lawful.
source: Central Insecticides Board & Registration Committee (CIBRC), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
verified_from: PIB Release 1896140, 3 February 2023 — 'Banning of Pesticides', Annexure, as on 01.10.2022

restricted.Aluminium Phosphide: Restricted: may be applied only by government-approved pest control operators under expert supervision. Tube packs of 10 and 20 tablets are banned outright.
restricted.Captafol: Restricted: banned as a foliar spray. Permitted only as a seed dresser.
restricted.Cypermethrin: Restricted: the 3% smoke generator may be used only through pest control operators, not by the general public.
restricted.DDT: Restricted: withdrawn from agriculture. Public health use only, under government supervision.
restricted.Fenitrothion: Restricted: banned in agriculture except for locust control in scheduled desert areas, and public health use.
restricted.Methyl Bromide: Restricted: may be applied only by government-approved pest control operators under expert supervision.
restricted.Monocrotophos: Restricted: banned for use on vegetables. Not banned on other crops.
restricted.Trifluralin: Restricted: all uses prohibited except on wheat. Toxic to aquatic life; keep away from water bodies.
